questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: Riya can read a printed page most distinctly, without any strain in her eyes, only when she holds it at a certain minimum distance from her eyes. State this distance for a young adult with normal vision, and give the name for this distance.

markingPoints.description: States the minimum distance of distinct vision as 25 cm (1)
Names it the least distance of distinct vision, or the near point of the eye (1)

answerScheme.modelAnswer: 25 cm; the least distance of distinct vision, also called the near point of the eye.

evidence:
To see an object comfortably and distinctly, you
must hold it at about 25 cm from the eyes.

For a young adult with normal vision, the near point is about
25 cm.

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: A girl steps out of a dark classroom into glaring afternoon sunlight, and soon the objects around her no longer look blurred. Name the dark muscular diaphragm that lies behind the cornea and controls the size of the pupil.

markingPoints.description: States that it is the dark muscular diaphragm behind the cornea controlling the size of the pupil (1)

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Iris; it controls the size of the pupil, and the pupil regulates the amount of light entering the eye.

evidence:
Iris is a dark muscular diaphragm that controls the
size of the pupil. The pupil regulates and controls the amount of light

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: An old man says that the world has become milky and hazy for him and that he can no longer make out faces clearly. Name the condition his eye lens has developed, and state how his vision can be restored.

markingPoints.description: States that vision can be restored through a cataract surgery (1)

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Cataract; vision can be restored through a cataract surgery.

evidence:
Sometimes, the crystalline lens of people at old age becomes milky and
cloudy. This condition is called cataract. This causes partial or complete
loss of vision. It is possible to restore vision through a cataract surgery.

questions.subject: Science
questions.topic: Dispersion of White Light by a Glass Prism
questions.stem: On a sunny day a student looks at the sky through the spray of a water fountain with the Sun behind him, and coloured bands appear overhead. State what causes these coloured bands, and the direction in which they always appear.

markingPoints.description: States that the colours are caused by the dispersion of sunlight by tiny water droplets, which act like small prisms (1)
States that the rainbow is always formed in a direction opposite to that of the Sun (1)

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Dispersion of sunlight by tiny water droplets, which act like small prisms; the rainbow is always formed in a direction opposite to that of the Sun.

evidence:
A rainbow is a natural spectrum appearing in the sky
after a rain shower (Fig. 10.7).

again when it comes out of the raindrop

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem:
Riya is reading a printed page in the evening. When she holds it very close to her eyes the letters look blurred and her eyes begin to strain, so she moves the page away until she can read it comfortably. She then looks out of the window at a tree far down the street and the leaves appear sharp. She notices that her eyes have made two different adjustments within a matter of seconds, and her brother tells her that a normal eye can see objects clearly only between a certain minimum distance and infinity.

Read the case below and answer the three questions that follow.
Riya is reading a printed page in the evening. When she holds it very close to her eyes the letters look blurred and her eyes begin to strain, so she moves the page away until she can read it comfortably. She then looks out of the window at a tree far down the street and the leaves appear sharp. She notices that her eyes have made two different adjustments within a matter of seconds, and her brother tells her that a normal eye can see objects clearly only between a certain minimum distance and infinity.
(i) State what happens to the curvature, the thickness and the focal length of the eye lens when Riya looks at the nearby page.
(ii) State the minimum distance at which a young adult with normal vision sees an object most distinctly without strain, and give the name for this distance.
(iii) Using what happens in each case, explain how the same eye manages to focus both on the nearby page and on the distant tree, and state the term for this ability.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (i) The ciliary muscles contract, so the lens becomes more curved and thicker and its focal length decreases. (ii) 25 cm; the least distance of distinct vision, or near point. (iii) The lens alters its focal length for each distance, decreasing it for the near page and increasing it for the distant tree. This ability is accommodation.

evidence:
When you are
looking at objects closer to the eye, the ciliary muscles contract. This
increases the curvature of the eye lens. The eye lens then becomes thicker.
Consequently, the focal length of the eye lens decreases.

To see an object comfortably and distinctly, you
must hold it at about 25 cm from the eyes.

The ability of the eye lens to adjust its focal length is called
accommodation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem:
Riya holds an arrow-shaped bookmark in front of her eye and looks at it. She is told that the light from the bookmark is bent as it enters her eye and that the lens system inside forms an image of the bookmark on a delicate light-sensitive membrane at the back of the eyeball. She is surprised to learn that this image is upside down. She also learns that most of the bending happens not at the lens but at the outer surface of the transparent membrane at the front of the eyeball, and that the lens only makes the finer adjustment of focal length needed for objects at different distances.

Read the case below and answer the three questions that follow.
Riya holds an arrow-shaped bookmark in front of her eye and looks at it. She is told that the light from the bookmark is bent as it enters her eye and that the lens system inside forms an image of the bookmark on a delicate light-sensitive membrane at the back of the eyeball. She is surprised to learn that this image is upside down. She also learns that most of the bending happens not at the lens but at the outer surface of the transparent membrane at the front of the eyeball, and that the lens only makes the finer adjustment of focal length needed for objects at different distances.
(i) Name the transparent membrane at the front of the eyeball at which most of the refraction of the entering light occurs, and state what the crystalline lens does.
(ii) State the nature of the image that the eye lens forms on the light-sensitive membrane at the back of the eyeball.
(iii) The image formed on that membrane is inverted, yet Riya sees the bookmark the right way up. Explain how this happens.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (i) The cornea; the crystalline lens provides the finer adjustment of focal length needed to focus objects at different distances. (ii) An inverted real image. (iii) The light-sensitive cells get activated and generate electrical signals which travel to the brain through the optic nerves, and the brain interprets them so that objects are perceived as they really are.

evidence:
Most of the
refraction for the light rays entering the eye
occurs at the outer surface of the cornea. The
crystalline lens merely provides the finer
adjustment of focal length required to focus

The eye lens forms an inverted real image of the object
on the retina.

These signals are
sent to the brain via the optic nerves. The brain interprets these signals,
and finally, processes the information so that we perceive objects as
they are.

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem:
Kamala is an elderly woman. Lately the objects around her look hazy and she says that the colours of the sky and of the green plants near her house have become difficult to tell apart. She can still manage to move about familiar rooms by touch and by the sounds they make, but she can no longer recognise her neighbours' faces. When she closes her eyes she can still tell what is on the table by its smell, but she cannot tell what colour anything is. Her family takes her to an eye doctor.

Read the case below and answer the three questions that follow.
Kamala is an elderly woman. Lately the objects around her look hazy and she says that the colours of the sky and of the green plants near her house have become difficult to tell apart. She can still manage to move about familiar rooms by touch and by the sounds they make, but she can no longer recognise her neighbours' faces. When she closes her eyes she can still tell what is on the table by its smell, but she cannot tell what colour anything is. Her family takes her to an eye doctor.
(i) Name the condition that has developed in Kamala's eye lens, and state what has happened to the lens.
(ii) State the effect this condition has on vision, and the treatment that can restore it.
(iii) Explain why Kamala can still identify things by their smell or by the sounds they make after her eyes have failed, but why she cannot identify colours.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (i) Cataract; the crystalline lens has become milky and cloudy. (ii) It causes partial or complete loss of vision, which can be restored through a cataract surgery. (iii) Smell, taste, sound and touch still work without sight, but colours can be identified only by the eye, so no other sense can take over.

evidence:
Sometimes, the crystalline lens of people at old age becomes milky and
cloudy. This condition is called cataract. This causes partial or complete
loss of vision. It is possible to restore vision through a cataract surgery.

closing the eyes, we can identify objects to some extent by their smell,
taste, sound they make or by touch. It is, however, impossible to identify
colours while closing the eyes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.topic: Dispersion of White Light by a Glass Prism
questions.stem:
Neel and his classmates set up an experiment for the school science exhibition. They made a narrow slit in a thick sheet of cardboard and allowed a narrow beam of sunlight to fall through it. A glass prism was then placed in the beam and turned slowly until the light coming out of it fell on a nearby screen. A band of seven colours appeared, and Neel wrote them down in order as Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange and Red. A visitor asked him why the colours of sunlight should appear separate at all.

Read the case below and answer the two questions that follow.
Neel and his classmates set up an experiment for the school science exhibition. They made a narrow slit in a thick sheet of cardboard and allowed a narrow beam of sunlight to fall through it. A glass prism was then placed in the beam and turned slowly until the light coming out of it fell on a nearby screen. A band of seven colours appeared, and Neel wrote them down in order as Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange and Red. A visitor asked him why the colours of sunlight should appear separate at all.
(i) State the reason why the colours of sunlight appear separate after passing through the prism, and give the name for the band of coloured components of the light beam.
(ii) A second identical prism is now placed in an inverted position with respect to the first prism. State what emerges from the other side of the second prism, and explain what this shows about sunlight.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (i) Different colours bend through different angles as they pass through the prism, red the least and violet the most, so the rays take different paths and become distinct; the band is the spectrum. (ii) A beam of white light emerges, showing that sunlight is made up of seven colours.

evidence:
Different colours
of light bend through different angles with
respect to the incident ray, as they pass
through a prism. The red light bends the least
while the violet the most.

light beam is called its spectrum. You might
not be able to see all the colours separately.

He found a beam of white light emerging
from the other side of the second prism.
